title: Cross-check solvers on one model

blocks.text: A pipeline at a water utility solves each night's pump-scheduling MILP with several solvers before it trusts the plan, as a correctness check. Every solver gets the same model. Each one returns a status and an objective value. When the solvers that claim optimality disagree, something is wrong with one of them (a solver that quietly changed the model, a bug in an adapter), and the pipeline must say which.

Write `suspects(results, rel_tol)` in `crosscheck.py`. `results` maps a solver's name to `(status, objective)`. Only results with status `"OPTIMAL"` are judged. Their **reference value** $`r`$ is the median of their objectives (Python's `statistics.median`). A solver $`k`$ with objective $`z_k`$ is a suspect when
Return the suspects' names, sorted. With no optimal result, return an empty list.

import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from crosscheck import suspects

# (status, objective) reported by each solver on one model.
runs = {"Lark": ("OPTIMAL", 1450.0), "Wren": ("OPTIMAL", 1450.0), "Finch": ("OPTIMAL", 1452.0),
        "Robin": ("TIME_LIMIT", 1300.0)}
print("tolerance 1e-6:", suspects(runs, 1e-6))
print("tolerance 0.01:", suspects(runs, 0.01))
print("Robin OPTIMAL at 1300, tolerance 0.01:", suspects({**runs, "Robin": ("OPTIMAL", 1300.0)}, 0.01))
print("no OPTIMAL runs:", suspects({"Lark": ("INFEASIBLE", 0.0)}, 1e-6))

cases.says: a solver whose optimal objective is far from the others' is named, and the agreeing ones are not
an objective too high is as suspect as one too low
one wild value does not drag the reference and make the agreeing solvers look wrong
a run that stopped at a limit is neither judged nor used to set the reference
a difference no larger than the tolerance is not suspect
